title: Silky Oak: Ancient Silky Oaks You Can Visit
meta_description: Not an oak at all, a protea relative from Australia. Three mapped, including a 32 metre giant in Brisbane and a disputed record in Barcelona.
intro:
Grevillea robusta is not an oak, and it is not related to any tree that uses the name. It belongs to the protea family alongside banksias, native to the rainforest fringe of eastern Australia, and the site has three mapped.

Brisbane's, in the species' own homeland, is 32 metres tall and roughly a century old, taller than almost any grevillea gets. Setubal's, in Portugal, flowers in spring with dense one-sided combs of orange, more like a bottlebrush than anything most people picture when they hear silky oak. Barcelona's carries the most disputed measurements of the three: a municipal register puts its girth at 4.1 metres, an independent 2017 measurement found barely half that.

The wood was once prized by cabinetmakers for a silvery figure in the grain, which is where the common name comes from.
